text:
Consultation launched on proposals to update fees for statutory Maritime and Coastguard Agency services
Proposals would ensure charges fairly reflect the cost of delivering essential maritime services.
The Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) is consulting on proposals to update and simplify fees to fund critical statutory services that underpin the safe operation of UK shipping.
Following a review, a proposed schedule of fees is being presented by the MCA today (23 November 2026) in a nine-week consultation.
The proposed changes would establish a fairer and more sustainable approach, with fees increasing in line with inflation since the MCA’s fees were last set. This would reduce the need for the taxpayer to subsidise the MCA’s services, while ensuring customers receive a good quality service and are charged in a fair manner.
The proposals would also simplify the charging structure and give customers greater certainty, including through set fees for some services and a more consistent approach to surveyors’ travel time.
MCA Director of Finance and Analysis Oliver Poxon said:
  Services provided by the MCA are vital to helping operators and seafarers work with confidence and to meet their legal responsibilities, protecting the marine environment and maintaining high standards of maritime safety.
We want the way we charge for these services to be fair, transparent and straightforward.
This update is an opportunity to reflect feedback from our customers and to reform and simplify the MCA’s fees while ensuring they are fair and support the sustainable delivery of services that are essential for the safety of the maritime industry and the general public.
The three main sets of services involved are: Survey and Inspection; Seafarer Training and Certification; and Registry of Shipping and Seamen.
The consultation will run until 24 January 2027. To find out more and comment, visit Proposed Merchant Shipping (Fees) Regulations 2028 - GOV.UK
Background:
As an Executive Agency within the Department for Transport, the MCA is bound by principles set out in the HM Treasury guidance. These stipulate that statutory fees for activities should be set at levels which aim to recover the full economic cost of work undertaken and at cost levels that avoid overcharging the consumer or providing subsidies at the taxpayer’s expense (potentially leading to waste through poorly targeted consumption).
